entities.summary:
Giovanni Jona-Lasinio, sometimes called Gianni Jona, is an Italian theoretical physicist, best known for his works on quantum field theory and statistical mechanics. He pioneered research concerning spontaneous symmetry breaking, and the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model is named after him. When Yoichiro Nambu received the Nobel Prize, Jona-Lasinio gave the Nobel Lecture in his place, as a recognition from Nambu for their joint work.

At present, he holds a faculty position in the Physics Department of Sapienza University of Rome, and is a full member of the Accademia dei Lincei. Giovanni Jona-Lasinio was a scientists & inventors from Florence (b. 1932, Florence). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jona-Lasinio's work on spontaneous symmetry breaking and the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model has had a significant impact on our understanding of quantum field theory and statistical mechanics. His contributions have influenced research in particle physics and condensed matter physics.
